record_type_quote: This follow-up study was conducted at least 6 months after the original protocol.

targets.authors: Duff MC, Gupta R, Hengst J, Tranel D, Cohen NJ
targets.title: The use of definite references signals declarative memory: Evidence from hippocampal amnesia
targets.evidence_quote: Of particular interest was how similar the use of definite initiating reference in the present study, when the familiar partners of the amnesia participants were the directors, when compared with our previous work ( Duff et al., in press ), when the amnesia participants were the directors.
targets.outcome_quote: The data displayed that the difference between amnesia and comparison pairs in the use of indefinite references observed in Duff et al. (in press) was not limited to the productions of the amnesia participants but also extended to their partners without brain damage.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly extend the original observed difference to communication partners and compare the role-switched new observations to their previous results.

reasoning: New observations collected at least six months later in the same pairs with roles switched retest the published finding about definite reference and amnesia. This is new data, not reanalysis. Duff et al. (2006) supplies the barrier protocol; the specific definite-reference finding being retested is attributed to Duff et al. (in press). Clark is background theory and coding framework. Target year is printed only as in press. Article identity and author list verified in XML front matter.
